author: rvolosatovs
body:
Closes https://github.com/profianinc/drawbridge/issues/119

This PR introduces a concept of a package (which is an overloaded term, but we can address naming/branding later). A package is a tree-like structure, e.g. a directory, containing an `Enarx.toml` and `main.wasm`.
`enarx` can execute either a package, using the contained `Enarx.toml` within its root or a WASM binary directly.

That means:
```
enarx deploy file:///path/to/my.wasm
```
is a valid invocation, as is
```
enarx deploy file:///path/to/my/package
```
Where `/path/to/my/package` is an absolute path to a local directory containing (at least) `Enarx.toml` and `main.wasm`

Similarly, `http` and `https` schemes are supported, e.g.
```
enarx deploy https://example.com/path/to/my.wasm
```

If the response of a GET request to specified URL has a `Content-Type` of:
- `application/wasm` (need to double check the media type, if one exists already) => it attempts to execute it
- `application/vnd.drawbridge.directory.v1+json` => it assumes it's a https://github.com/profianinc/drawbridge tree directory and attempts to fetch `main.wasm` and `Enarx.toml` from the node rooted at specified URL.

Other media types, and schemes may be supported in the future.

In pure-WASM execution mode (i.e. not a package), the default config is implicitly used.

Apart from that, the PR adds a two-way communication channel between the exec layer and the host binary via unnamed Unix sockets. Potentially this could be used to send e.g. logs or errors to the host if desired. A TOML-encoded config is sent once on the socket by the host.

For uploading to Drawbridge, use:
```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -ex

# Create repository
curl --fail-with-body -sX PUT -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}' "localhost:8080/${1}"

# Create tag
curl --fail-with-body -sX PUT -H "Content-Type: application/vnd.drawbridge.entry.v1+json" -d '{"digest":{}}' "localhost:8080/${1}/_tag/${2}"

# Upload package
curl --fail-with-body -sX PUT -H "Content-Type: application/vnd.drawbridge.directory.v1+json" -d '{"Enarx.toml":{"digest":{}},"main.wasm":{"digest":{}}}' "localhost:8080/${1}/_tag/${2}/tree"

# Upload workload
curl --fail-with-body -sX PUT -H "Content-Type: application/wasm" -T "${3}" "localhost:8080/${1}/_tag/${2}/tree/main.wasm"

# Upload config
curl --fail-with-body -sX PUT -H "Content-Type: application/toml" -T "${4}" "localhost:8080/${1}/_tag/${2}/tree/Enarx.toml"
```

author: eandrewjones
body:
## Changes

I have moved many of the new environment variables into an encryption-decryption approach to work around the 4kb limit Amazon lambda function restrictions place on Vercel.

See: [https://vercel.com/support/articles/how-do-i-workaround-vercel-s-4-kb-environment-variables-limit](https://vercel.com/support/articles/how-do-i-workaround-vercel-s-4-kb-environment-variables-limit)

All new environment variables should follow this approach. In fact, environment variables is misnomer because these no longer need to be added to the local env file nor Vercel's environment variables. Instead, you must follow the workflow below:

1. Store related variables in a common JSON object and add it to `envVars.json` (to be circulated privately) with a proper nested namespace. For example:
```
{
        "retriever_bing_header_key_tag": "<variable>",
        "retriever_bing_header_key_value": "<variable>",
        "retriever_bing_search_url": "<variable>"
 }
```
2. Encrypt the object using a tool like [this](https://www.javainuse.com/aesgenerator), making sure to pass in the proper `secret` and `iv` (found in the `.env` file).
3. Store the returned string in `env/serviceAccount.enc.js` with the same key name used in `envVars.json`.
4. Decrypt the value in `utils/constants/global.ts` using the `decryptAES` utility function.

These values can then be imported wherever they are needed. The only exception is middleware files since nextJS middleware does not support importing modules anywhere in the call stack.

### Acceptance Criteria

New/modified functionality to test:

-  [ ] The demo account AI api call should work properly
-  [ ] The posts should not be visible from other users accounts

These are the only places where the site relies on env vars I've switched over to the new approach. We can leave the firebase, auth0 and any essential env vars as is.
 
### Branching / JIRA

-   [x] I have named this PR in the following format: [JIRA-ISSUE-NUMBER] - [description of the work done in this PR]
-   [x] I have created this PR through the following steps:

1. Fetched latest version of main (`git checkout main`)
3. Rebased my branch onto main if there are new updates to main (`git pull upstream main`->`git checkout main`->`git rebase main`)
4. Fixed any conflicts before pushing branch to main and creating PR

-   [x] I will follow the above steps every time I push new commits after review

author: sedghi
body:
We will start by looking at the style hierarchy. The style hierarchy is as follow.

- Annotation-level settings (with UID) **set/getAnnotationToolStyle**
  - Viewport-level tool settings **set/getViewportToolStyle**
    - Per-tool this layer: Length on this viewport
    - Global this layer: All tools in this viewport
      - toolGroup settings (for any tool specified in this toolGroup in all viewports of the toolGroup) **set/getToolGroupToolStyle**
        - Per-tool layer: Angle on this toolGroup in all viewports
        - Global this layer: All tools in this toolGroup in all viewports
          - Default level: **set/getDefaultToolStyle**
            - Per-tool layer (Length) settings
            - Global (app-level) settings (we provide a default).

In annotation rendering loop, upon getting a style for a certain property (`color`, `lineDash`, `lineThickness`)
we check whether the style is set at the annotation level (highest priority).
If not, we check whether any viewport-level setting is set (for the viewport annotation is drawing on); however,
in the viewportLevel, we first check whether the tool-level setting is set. If not, we check in the "global" (all tools in the viewport) level.
If not found, we move to the next level for toolGroup level. If not found, we move to the next level for global level which is last
level to check.

- Add Drag probe 
- Fix a bug where textlines changing would not appear

author: rtschmitz
body:
#### PR description:

This PR adds one RECO level skim that saves all standard AOD collections. This PR is similar to [PR#37509](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/37509), which added a skim over delayed jets using a set of HLT paths, except this skim uses a cut on MET rather than on HT. It does this using the producer/filter for delayed jets in CMSSW and skimming over the HLT path "HLT_PFMET120_PFMHT120_IDTight_v*".

Tested with high-Pt QCD samples /store/relval/CMSSW_12_3_0_pre6/RelValQCD_Pt_1800_2400_14/GEN-SIM-RECO/123X_mcRun3_2021_realistic_v11-v2/, the skimmed AOD file size was 25MB (68 events) and the unskimmed AOD file size was 1.9GB (9000 events).

#### PR validation:

Ran with CMSSW_12_4_0_pre1 and used the config file "test_DelayedJetMET_cfg.py" which is included in this PR.

author: bryan-aguilar
body:
**Description:** Adds timeout and retry functionality to `terraform apply` steps. By default this will only retry once but that can be tweaked if necssary. 

Timeout was displaying a weird behavior where two interrupt signals were sent despite only logging one. This can be seen through this log during testing.
```
timeout: sending signal INT to command ‘terraform’
Stopping operation...

Interrupt received.
Please wait for Terraform to exit or data loss may occur.
Gracefully shutting down...


Two interrupts received. Exiting immediately. Note that data loss may have occurred.

╷
│ Error: operation canceled
│ 
│ 
```
I have found correspondence that this may be due to the version I am using for `coreutils` [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66518048/double-signal-send-with-command-timeout). This could cause an issue since the ubuntu vm uses `coreutils` version `8.30-3ubuntu2` but it is unknown without testing on the workflow itself. 

**Testing:** Tested on local machine with tests that were guaranteed to fail. Set timeout very low to test timeout and retry mechanic at the same time. 

Fixes #668

author: frouioui
body:
This Pull Request contains various enhancements and bug fixes that improve the overall stability of the benchmarking results.

The list of things that are modified is:
- Temporarily removed the molecule tests from the CI. Better end-to-end tests will be written in a follow-up PR.
- Changed the macro-benchmark topology from `6 vtgates - 2 vttablets` to `3 vtgates - 4 vttablets (primary/replica in each shard)`
- Removed debugging in Ansible tasks
- Make sure the `vitess` user and group are created in the new benchmarking server
- Use the same storage device during micro and macro benchmarks
- Format properly the storage device between each benchmark
- Make sure to kill the `arewefastyetcli` processes before and after a benchmark
- Make sure to kill all `sysbench` processes before and after a benchmark
- Fixed equality issue with `ansible_os_family`
- Added support for `go1.18.1`
- Support the new flag syntax of `vtctlclient`
- Removed the `-gateway_implementation` flag from vtgate's service configuration
- Changed the default OLTP and TPCC sysbench configuration to have smaller and more reliable benchmarks
- Addition of a new CRON schedule for the tags/releases benchmarks
- Increased the timeout for microbenchmarks from 2 to 4 hours
- Fixed an issue in the results compare where only one result was compared with the current benchmark instead of all the results that need to be compared
- Avoid the duplication of Pull Request CRON benchmarks
- Fixed the main `cron` web page to show results from `today` (included) to `today - 31 days`
- Capped the minimum version of Vitess for tags/releases benchmark to `v12.0.0`
- Avoid running profiling for micro-benchmarks unless told otherwise by a newly introduced flag
- Fixed configuration issue in influxdb's ansible role
- Encrypt Grafana's secrets in Ansible

author: phlexpay
body:
Presently when an anonymous type is created the fields are marked as readonly.  This is helpful in certain scenarios because the ultimate type is immutable and can be tracked much easier.  However it removes the ability to use anonymous types as a full-fidelity complex structure for passing around data in a program.  
The common alternative, Dictionary<string,object> works fine in certain scenarios but suffers in areas where data binding is required.  The lack of this basic feature forces developers to create a class for every single complex data structure that needs to be passed around - even if all that structure will ever be is data.

author: stoutput
body:
Masonite should not cast args to strings when compiling SQL, or when checking if some data exists in a collection. Rather it should use the raw data that was passed (`where()` already does this), and not make assumptions about what kind of data it is. Special cases should be handled manually, such as numeric strings matching integers.

This allows for using data such as bytes objects as args to `where_in` clauses, which will now correctly match against all database-supported data types.

This _may_ break some callers (that expect string coercion), so it should probably be considered backward-incompatible.

author: github-learning-lab[bot]
body:
# Using `request changes` on a pull request Thanks again for all your help on that last pull request. With our powers combined, _anything_ is possible! This next change might introduce some new changes that aren't going to look great. Sometimes, the author might identify that something isn't working. They might need a helping hand :wave: to solve the problem. In other instances, it might only work in their environment. When reviewing a pull request, look at and test the code to pinpoint any bugs or unexpected behavior. ### Writing a review #### Review the `diff` Reviewing the `diff`, the comparison of the proposed code, in the context of the whole project. Could it introduce performance problems, or security vulnerabilities? Try to predict unintended consequences that this change could cause. #### Try it out For most things, actually trying out the proposed change is a good idea. This makes it a lot easier to tell if the actual change matches the intention. You can do this by: - Cloning the repository, and checking out to the branch compared in the pull request. Run the application in your local development environment. - Deploying the pull request to a review-lab or staging environment (as appropriate). When summarizing your review, let the author know if you completed any of these tests. #### Empathy and Constructive Feedback The goal of providing feedback on a pull request is to ensure that the best possible change is being added. Sometimes, a change isn't addressing the problem in the best possible way. It's the reviewer's responsibility to provide meaningful and constructive feedback. ### Requesting Changes 101 Before you submit your review, your line comments are pending and only visible to you. You can edit pending comments anytime before you submit your review. To cancel a pending review and its pending comments, scroll down to the end of the page in the Conversation tab. Then click **Cancel review**. ## Step 4: Leave a review that asks for changes If you could check out this code for me and tell me what is wrong, that would be fantastic. ### :keyboard: Activity: Requesting changes 1. On the pull request, click **Files changed** 1. Hover over the line of code where you'd like to add a comment, and click the blue comment icon 1. In the comment window, type your comment 1. Click **Start a review** - If you have already started a review, you can click **Add review comment** 1. Above the changed code, click **Review changes** 1. Type a comment summarizing your feedback on the proposed changes - _Note: The problem here is that too many Tetris pieces are the same color. In your review, you might want to suggest that I choose colors which would be easier to see when playing the game._ 1. Select **Request changes** to submit feedback introducing changes necessary before merging 1. Click **Submit review**

Return to this pull request for my next comment

> _Sometimes I respond too fast for the page to update! If you perform an expected action and don't see a response, wait a few seconds and refresh the page for your next steps._

<!--
Thank you for contributing to TiDB-CDC! Please read MD's [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb-cdc/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document **BEFORE** filing this PR.
-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--
Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.
 -->

Issue Number: ref #4423 

### What is changed and how it works?
For the DDLs involving more than one table such as `RENAME TABLE`, `DROP TABLE` and `DROP VIEW`, TiCDC will dispatch the DDL events to the corresponding Kafka topics respectively if the table-level topic dispatch rules are configured.

But there exist some subtle difference between `RENAME TABLE` and the other two `DROP` statements.
- For `RENAME TABLE` statement, only one DDL job will be generated, so we must parse the DDL events from that job.
- For `DROP TABLE` and `DROP VIEW` statements, multiple DDL jobs containing **different** table/view info will be generated for each statement. But the query in those jobs are **identical** to each other. Thus we must rebuild the correct query.

author: marcboudreau
body:
This PR overhauls the integration tests suite for this project.

The new integration test suite is driven from a Go test function and requires a Kubernetes cluster (such as Docker-Desktop) to be available to run Vault servers in Pods and Jobs for running **hvc** with each test case.

The Go test function begins by applying 2 different Terraform projects through the terratest packages.  The first Terraform project (contained in the *tests/setup/* directory) sets up the Pods and related Kubernetes resources for the target and source Vault servers.  The second Terraform project (contained in the *tests/configure/* directory) configures all required resources within the Vault servers: secrets in the source Vault server and Kubernetes authentication method in both Vault servers.  This second project also configures Kubernetes ConfigMap resources for each test case, each containing the test case's copy job specification file.

Next, the Go test function sequentially runs each test case.  The test case consists of creating a Kubernetes Job to run the **hvc** application with the copy job spec mounted from the corresponding ConfigMap resource.  Once the job completes, various assertions are executed to verify that the expected outcome of the test case is met.

# New methods for `EntryStore`

Additional methods required for replication logic.

```rust
  async fn get_entry_by_hash(
      &self,
      hash: &Hash,

  async fn try_get_backlink(
      &self,

      &self,

      &self,

      seq_num: &SeqNum,
      max_number_of_entries: usize,

      log_id: LogId,

) -> Result<Vec<StorageEntry>, EntryStoreError>;

author: usernamefodder
body:
There's no reason why resymgen shouldn't support 64-bit binaries, and as
a somewhat general-purpose tool it's arguably expected that it should.
Change Uint to u64 to allow this, and add a few tests to make sure
things still work with numbers larger-than-32-bit numbers.
    
Users working with 32-bit binaries should not be meaningfully affected
by this increase in maximum value, since specifying both the address and
length for each symbol block is already required, and should constrain
symbol addresses and lengths to 32-bit integers via the in-bounds
symbols check resymgen provides, even when the underlying Uint type is
u64.

body:
## Summary

These repatriates gas fees from contract authors.

It effectively adds a hook into pre_dispatch so that we can check for the call type, and if the call type is a call to the contracts pallet, we append the author data there.

Then it gets passed to the Unbalance handler in `account-manager` if the call has some beneficiary, and sends the adjusted gas fees to the beneficiary.

This should be super easy for `pallet-evm` when we do 3VM Level 3.

Due to the way that balances and `tx-payment` are designed, those traits are not in frame_support. So we need to have a macro which we define in `account-manager`, so that we don't copy-paste this. 

Also fixes some lints.

author: weiznich
body:
This was triggered by the fact that the pool tries to open a new
connection after the old one was closed. As this happens in a background
thread this happens concurrently to our test code. That means if
establishing a new connection is fast that will increase the
acquire_count before we checked it. We observed this happening for
sqlite. I've opted into just not checking the acquire count there as
this is not really relevant anyway at that point.

I assume the intent with the flash is to survive redirects. For example a POST handler sets an error message, redirects to another page, and the GET to that page reads the flash.

As this takes what was previously only a runtime check and moves it to a compile-time check, we believe that it should be functionally equivalent to prior releases, but if you run into problems, please let us know by opening an issue. [#3037]

    What's New

    • workbox-webpack-plugin has been rewritten in TypeScript, and has public TypeScript definitions for its interfaces published as part of this release. We do not anticipate any changes in the underlying functionality as part of this rewrite. [#2882]
    • A forceSyncFallback parameter has been added to workbox-background-sync, without changing the default behavior. When forceSyncFallback is explicitly set to true, workbox-background-sync will always attempt to replay queued requests when the service worker starts up and never rely on the sync event listener. Most developers will not need this behavior, but it can be useful when targeting environments that have a non-functional Background Sync implementation, like some Electron runtimes. [#3020]

body:
Currently if the runner process crashes before it connects to the host
(e.g. because an import fails on missing dependency), we don't see
stdout/err unless DEVELOPMENT is set. This makes it hard to debug some
situations (e.g. https://app.clickup.com/t/24308805/SCP-3676).

The new approach is to save all output to a file and show it in case of
failure.

We could also:
- consider saving the logs only for some time
- displaying only last N lines in case of failure
- try to detect when runner tcp connection is established and stop capturing logs then
- somehow give logfiles more meaningful names (with PID/container ID?)

What do you think?

# Using `request changes` on a pull request Thanks again for all your help on that last pull request. With our powers combined, _anything_ is possible! This next change might introduce some new changes that aren't going to look great. Sometimes, the author might identify that something isn't working. They might need a helping hand :wave: to solve the problem. In other instances, it might only work in their environment. When reviewing a pull request, look at and test the code to pinpoint any bugs or unexpected behavior. ### Writing a review #### Review the `diff` Reviewing the `diff`, the comparison of the proposed code, in the context of the whole project. Could it introduce performance problems, or security vulnerabilities? Try to predict unintended consequences that this change could cause. #### Try it out For most things, actually trying out the proposed change is a good idea. This makes it a lot easier to tell if the actual change matches the intention. You can do this by: - Cloning the repository, and checking out to the branch compared in the pull request. Run the application in your local development environment. - Deploying the pull request to a review-lab or staging environment (as appropriate). When summarizing your review, let the author know if you completed any of these tests. #### Empathy and Constructive Feedback The goal of providing feedback on a pull request is to ensure that the best possible change is being added. Sometimes, a change isn't addressing the problem in the best possible way. It's the reviewer's responsibility to provide meaningful and constructive feedback. ### Requesting Changes 101 Before you submit your review, your line comments are pending and only visible to you. author: jsnajdr
body:
Fixes https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/55628 by avoiding an unwanted side effect of changes done in https://core.trac.wordpress.org/ticket/55250

That patch stopped printing translations inline scripts when these translations were empty, removing some bloat from the generated HTML. But that change also had another effect that turned out to be unwanted. When the `print_translations` method returns `true` for a script, the script won't be concatenated with `load-scripts.php`. But now `print_translations` started returning `false`, starting to concatenate scripts like `common`, which, during registration in `wp_default_scripts`, are marked as "having translations," which means "using `wp-18n` and translations from the `default` domain," without actually providing any translations:
```php
$scripts->add( 'common', "/wp-admin/js/common$suffix.js", array( 'jquery', 'hoverIntent', 'utils' ), false, 1 );
$scripts->set_translations( 'common' );
```
Then, when `common` got concatenated and `wp-i18n`, having been overridden by Gutenberg plugin, wasn't concatenated (because scripts from plugins are not), they were loaded in reversed order and the `common` script crashed with a reference error accessing `wp.i18n.__`.

The solution is to reinstate the concatenation opt-out condition with checking if `$obj->textdomain` is set. That way, we can eat our cake (avoid outputting redundant scripts) and keep it too (prevent concatenation).

author: mbehzad
body:
# Switch do dart-sass instead of node-sass for processing .scss files

Dart Sass is currently the active implementation of sass and gets new features. It is stable for a long time now, and imo it makes sense to switch to it.

## Pros

- allows usage of modern CSS syntax. For example `width: min(100px, 10vw);` instead of weird workaround via interpolations: `#{"width: min(100px, 10vw);"}`
- Better modularization possibilities
- node-sass binaries are tied to the node version which means changing node version is coupled to the need of re-downloading node-sass binaries. etc.

## Cons

- not being able to use `/` for division. e.g.
```scss
// node-sass
width: 100% / 3;


// dart-sass
@use "sass:math" as *;

width: div(100%, 3);

// or use the browser to do the job:
width: calc(100% / 3);
```

There is a [sass-migrator](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/cli/migrator) cli tool which can help automatically update the codebase.

- it compiles noticeably slower (e.g. on a ~50 components repo it took 1.5 -2 times to compile the scss compared to the current node-sass)
But once sass-loader can use the native Dart Sass executable, this would be less relevant (see https://github.com/webpack-contrib/sass-loader/issues/774).

## Breaking?

Technically it would probably compile successfully our code bases so it isn't a breaking change. But that will generate a lot of deprecation warnings regarding the usage of slash for division.
 see https://sass-lang.com/documentation/breaking-changes for possible breaking changes

## User preference

It is also possible to allow the user to choose between these two sass implementation by:

1- property in `pv.config.js`
2- sass not being a direct dependency of pv-script, and the user has to install `node-sass` or `sass` themselves. (similar to CRA which we have its error message already in [formatWebpackMessages.js#L79](https://github.com/pro-vision/fe-tools/blob/develop/packages/pv-scripts/helpers/formatWebpackMessages.js#L79)




== Closes issue(s) ==


== Changes ==


== Affected Packages ==
pv-scripts

author: madelson
body:
This avoids compilation errors based on target framework.

Fix #24909

Right now, there are several cases where ImplicitUsings doesn't work "out of the box" if you are not targeting the latest framework version available in the current SDK. With this approach, we ensure that the default set of implicit usings should not cause compilation errors because each namespace is at least minimally defined.

The biggest downside I see to this approach is that if someone customizes the ImplicitUsings list and they misspell the namespace, they would no longer get a compilation error alerting them to that fact.

An alternative solution to this would be carefully selecting the set of default namespaces based on the lowest-common-denominator set available in the referenced target frameworks.

body:
After installation, this plugin creates a file called output.log which is publicly accessible if the web server is not explicitly configured to block direct access to this type of file.

Consequently I have added a file called .htaccess which, for users using Apache web server, allows direct public access only to images, fonts, js and css files specific to this plugin.

So it restricts direct public access to files like config.json, output.log, readme.txt, LICENSE.md, etc.

This is a similar configuration to that used by Akismet in their open source plugin. See details here: https://github.com/wp-plugins/akismet/blob/master/.htaccess


In addition I added the docker_tag file and the xdebug and .vscode folders to the list of files and folders that are ignored when creating a new package that is distributed on WordPress.org.

Adds firmware endpoint to ServerService. This endpoint will be used by two services:
 - The firmware syncer service which will be responsible for populating the data in the `component_firmware_version` table.
 - The inventory collection service which will set the component data during inventory collection (both out of band and in band). The component data model will be updated as part of https://packet.atlassian.net/browse/SE-373 and it should include foreign keys to the `component_firmware_version` for the current and desired firmware versions.

author: troopa81
body:
This PR fixes Clazy check (the ones we target in *CLAZY_BASE_CHECKS* cmake variable) and make them blocking for the CI.

I deleted the following checks: 
- *lambda-in-connect*: I think we will get only false positives because we use it with with a QEventLoop::exec() so the captured variable never reach end of scope before the lambda is called
- *qcolor-from-literal*: It crashes clang with clazy 1.11, so I commented for now, but maybe in the future we could add it again
- *qobject-macro*: I think it's useless to add a QOBJECT macro all the time because it increase compile time and it's not needed for all classes
- *non-pod-global-static*. It's temporary, I plan to revive it in a separate PR.

Regarding *skipped-base-class*, I added a skip instruction in code ([here](lien?) and all classes extending QgsBasicNumericFormat) because it would change behavior (sortKey is 100 in QgsNumericFormat vs 1 in QgsBasicNumericFormat). I'm not sure this is intended behavior? @nyalldawson ?

* manage python requirements using requirements-menu.txt
* more reliable (installs exact versions of all dependencies)
* is completely separate from any system-wide installed python packages,
  won't conflict with existing installed python packages.
* minimizes global system requirements down to python and python-virtualenv

virtualenv requires "--seed pip" or pip will fail with:
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pip._internal.utils'`
If anyone knows why, I'd be interested to hear.

Fixes  #499, Fixes #390

author: franpeza
body:
## Problem

We are planning to add some functionality to the project, so it would be nice to make sure the env is the most updated possible, so with this PR we're trying to help with this :)

## Changes

- `eslint` libraries were being listed as dependencies but not config was set. So an eslint config was added.
- Same thing with `prettier`, it was listed as a dependency and executed on commit (not configured for ts files though) but some files were not formatted with it.
- Some unused dependencies were removed from both `dependencies` and `devDependencies`.
- Removed react-hot-loader because it was not proper configured. I have already a working version with [react-refresh-webpack-plugin](https://github.com/pmmmwh/react-refresh-webpack-plugin) planned for a future PR.
- Some libraries (mostly for the frontend part compilation) were upgrades in order to `improve` the generation of the bundle.
- Some `general cleanup`: removed unused imports, unused declarations, etc.

It could seem like a lot of changes but most of them are styling modifications :)

## Testing

- Both tests and functional tests pass, so they were not affected as expected.
- All commands in package.json works as before the modifications.
- The app compiles and runs both locally and in Docker as expected, so nothing was broken.

author: maxwipfli
body:
On Linux, the user agent includes 'X11; Ubuntu; Linux ${arch}'.

On my non-Ubuntu Linux machine, the UA used is almost identical, except
for the 'Ubuntu; ' part. Removing that part from the default UA we use
fixes that particular error and seems no to break any other services.

#### Pre-flight Checklist

#### Description of Change
Removed `Ubuntu; ` from the user agent generated on Linux machines.

#### Motivation and Context
The user agent string breaks the Google Calendar service because the server decides to serve to mobile site instead of the desktop site based on that string.

Removing the `Ubuntu; ` brings the UA in line with what my Chrome is using on a non-Ubuntu Linux machine. This also makes the UA "more correct" since not everybody using Linux is on Ubuntu. This fixes the issue and seems to not break anything else.

I think this is a sensible change to make here instead of using a "custom" user agent for the `googlecalendar` recipe.

author: bitdivine
body:
# Motivation
We need better control over environment variable based configuration.  `process.env.` values are accessed across the svelte codebase, making it hard to verify that they are parsed and interpreted consistently.

The control is needed:
- For deploying to new environments, such as localhost without the proxy or new testnets.
- For deploying production-like builds to testnets.

A small goal in this direction is therefore to access the environment only in constants files, ideally in environment.constants.ts unless there are strong compelling reasons to use another constants file.

# Changes
- Defined a lint rule to enforce the policy.
- Moved any direct access of process.env to the environment.constants file.

In cases where clock skew or timezone issues are preventing backup label generation the user could see an error like this:

new backup label '20220504-152308F' is not later than latest backup label '20220504-222042F_20220504-222141I.manifest.gz'

This will happen if the most recent label is drawn from the history. It is cleaner (and probably less confusing) to strip off the extensions so the user sees:

new backup label '20220504-152308F' is not later than latest backup label '20220504-222042F_20220504-222141I'

With quantum_glasses.py, a user can have access to a Tkinter app that provides single-qubit state transition visualization via a simple function call. author: mgaonach
body:
This PR allows:

- Build a new image when a GitHub release is created and push it to `ispyb/ispyb-pydb` on docker-hub with a version tag matching the release tag.
- Make a new version release and bump version number when new code is merged into `main` branch, which will trigger image publish.
  - Bumps minor version number by default, possibility to change it with labels on the PR : `norelease`, `release:major`, `release:minor`, or `release:patch` (more info https://github.com/rymndhng/release-on-push-action).
  - This version number is mirrored to the image version umber, which will allow us to pin the version number we want to have in the tests, and increase it in a new version of the tests only once we have verified that this version of the test works with this version of the DB.

## Description

<!-- Describe your changes in detail. -->
Delete the workspace and HOME directories at the end of GitHub Actions test runs.

## Motivation and context

<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
The self-update process on the self-hosted GitHub Actions runners fails to restart the runner. The only error I see in the logs is: `Access to the path '/home/azure/actions-runner/_work/_temp/_github_home/.nv' is denied.`. This path is owned by root because GitHub Actions bind mounts `/home/azure/actions-runner/_work/_temp/_github_home/` as the home directory, then runs jobs in the container as root. This process is hard coded in the runner and is not configurable.

This fix cleans up all files that could be made as the docker root user before exiting so that error should not longer occur.

## Description

This rule rewrites the function signature to a single line when possible (e.g. when not exceeding the "max_line_length" property) or a multiline signature otherwise. In case of function with a body expression, the body expression is placed on the same line as the function signature when not exceeding the "max_line_length" property. Optionally the function signature can be forced to be written as a multiline signature in case the function has more than a specified number of parameters (".editorconfig" property "ktlint_function_signature_wrapping_rule_always_with_minimum_parameters")

Fixed the FunctionStartOfBodySpacingRule to add the missing space before start of the block body before the BLOCK element type instead of as first element inside the BLOCK element.

author: gmaretic
body:
**Goals (and why)**:
==COMMIT_MSG==
Transactions_3 now has proper concurrency controls when reading a staging value.
==COMMIT_MSG==

Previously, on reading a staging value in the transactions table, we would do a CAS to touch the value, followed by a PUT. When multiple transactions were trying to read the same value, this would result in concurrent competing CAS (even though they were semantically the same), which could quickly explode and could continue going on even after a successful PUT.

**Implementation Description (bullets)**:
We do the following:
- we ensure only a single touch is in flight at any moment in time for the transactions service
- we coalesce concurrent TOUCH + PUT requests for the same start timestamp
- we cache the result of recent TOUCH + PUT requests, so only a single instance actually causes KVS calls, in absence of failure

This is done through a combination of synchronisation and a loading cache: when we need to do a TOUCH and a PUT in the protocol, the TOUCH is synchronised, preventing parallel CAS on the KVS level. The loading cache coalesces concurrent calls for the same timestamp and, if successful, also avoids future calls for that timestamp by shortcutting to the result of the cache lookup. 
**Testing (What was existing testing like?  What have you done to improve it?)**:
Existing tests + added tests that exercise the behaviour: coalescing of concurrent requests, serialising CASs, not doing unnecessary touches or puts.

**Concerns (what feedback would you like?)**:
Tests are implementation dependent, but they do test an implementation detail, so some amount of it is hard to avoid. I did add some docs warnings if changes are made that might invalidate them. Also, tests now look ugly because they were written before the inter-rim "fix", but we can live with that probably.

This is probably the best we can do short of implementing a batch CAS endpoint in Cassandra. The risk here is that if we manage to read so many distinct staging start timestamps that we cannot serially do the touches fast enough, we will start falling behind. I do not think this is a realistic issue as once the original commit's PUT goes through, it will unblock all further reads for that start timestamp, even if there are touches waiting on the lock, but definitely worth a short discussion.

**Where should we start reviewing?**:
ResilientCommitTimestampPutUnlessExistsTable

**Priority (whenever / two weeks / yesterday)**:
🔥 but we also need to be careful...

body:
### Changelog category (leave one):
- New Feature

### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md):
This PR enables `POPULATE` for WindowView. 

Examples are in `01073_window_view_event_tumble_to_asc_populate`, `01074_window_view_event_tumble_asc_join_populate` and `01075_window_view_proc_tumble_to_now_populate`. 

1. `POPULATE` is mainly used in event time processing because the data generated in the past will not be processed at processing time.
2. When using `POPULATE`, the original data in the source table will be sorted with the timestamp column so that all data can be processed. For example, the first row with a very large timestamp will cause the rest data outdated. But sorting is not a good solution, because the order of the data has been changed, this can be updated in the future.

![download](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9844978/166964709-7cfaae20-90f8-44c4-a7b8-77d41a5a2c5d.png)

With the current code, it is not possible for the user to see and differentiate between different types of bans. Also it is not possible to see when the ban will be resolved (which was available in WW1).

With this PR coins (UTXO) can have two types of ban. Normal and long ban. Prison stores the punishment type in class InMate and WabiSabi config delivers the timeouts for resolving the ban. 

This is a priority because it will slightly change the protocol.

Node `can_process()` will throw an error when the node is inside tree.
When you have a Tween with `TWEEN_PAUSE_BOUND` and tween a node that leaves tree, you will get spammed with this error, because the Tween will try to determine whether it can process and poll a node that isn't inside tree.

This was left unnoticed for a long time, until #56648 changed the default pause mode.

author: krasznaa
body:
After a **lot** of preparations, this is the 1000lb gorilla that I was talking about since a while...

I created a common implementation for the doublet finding between the CUDA and SYCL libraries. There are a lot of updates here, so let me try to just highlight some stuff:
  - I added a common type of doublet counter, which required steps after the doublet finding to be updated as well. Which is one reason why I ended up touching so many files.
  - Instead of letting the device threads figure out which elements of the input jagged vectors they should work with (through the `traccc::cuda::cuda_helper::find_idx_on_jagged_vector`, `traccc::cuda::cuda_helper::find_idx_on_container`, `traccc::sycl::sycl_helper::find_idx_on_jagged_vector` and `traccc::sycl::sycl_helper::find_idx_on_container` functions), the doublet counting and doublet finding kernels now use host-created prefix sums for this purpose instead.
    * Making use of the previously introduced `traccc::device::get_prefix_sum` helper function.
  - I removed the thread-synchronization/collaboration from the doublet finding kernels. The way that shared memory is used there at the moment for slightly reducing the number of atomic updates into global memory just didn't seem to make a lot of sense/difference for me. But @beomki-yeo may very well disaggree.
    * I further delayed the introduction of dealing with thread synchronisation in a uniform way in these shared functions like this. But I do have ideas for how to implement thread synchronisation uniformly between CUDA and SYCL if/when the time comes.

Finally, just to show that the updates don't make things worse. In fact, they make the seed finding a little faster. (The absolute values are not too relevant, but all measurements between the old/current and new codes were done on the same hardware. So the relative values are meaningful.)

| υ | Current CUDA | New CUDA | Current SYCL | New SYCL |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| 10 | 0.0456415 | 0.0353137 | 0.160323 | 0.0521146 |
| 40 | 0.0552883 | 0.0429054 | 0.258301 | 0.0871926 |
| 80 | 0.0665741 | 0.0558218 | 0.31336 | 0.12144 |
| 140 | 0.0904985 | 0.0809856 | 0.383457 | 0.169536 |
| 200 | 0.117286 | 0.107773 | 0.443463 | 0.217447 |

As you can see, one of my main motivations for all this harmonisation is that the SYCL code is a lot slower by now. Not having received a number of updates that Beomki made in the CUDA code. Hopefully once all kernels are harmonised in this way, the performance numbers will be a lot closer to each other...

I'm curious what everybody will think. :wink:

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>slackapi/java-slack-sdk</summary>

### [`v1.22.0`](https://togithub.com/slackapi/java-slack-sdk/releases/v1.22.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/slackapi/java-slack-sdk/compare/v1.21.2...v1.22.0)

##### New Features

##### Message Metadata (Open Beta) Support

[Message Metadata](https://api.slack.com/metadata) is a new feature in the Slack Platform, which enables developers to link a message inside Slack to a corresponding outside event or pattern.

With this Java SDK, you can post a message with metadata as below:

```java
String token = System.getenv("SLACK_BOT_TOKEN");
MethodsClient client = Slack.getInstance().methods(token);
// Post a message with metadata

// You can set any type of data under the event_payload part
Map<String, Object> eventPayload = new HashMap<>();
eventPayload.put("procurement-id", "id-123");
eventPayload.put("amount", 1024);
eventPayload.put("tags", Arrays.asList("Procurement", "Engineering Division"));

// Build the metadata to attach to your app's message
Message.Metadata metadata = Message.Metadata.builder()
  .eventType("internal-procurement-approval")
  .eventPayload(eventPayload)
  .build();

// Post a channel message with the metadata
ChatPostMessageResponse resposne = client.chatPostMessage(req -> req
  .channel("#random")
  .text("Can you approve this procurement process request?")
  .metadata(metadata));
```

Once your app post a message with metadata, your app (and other apps too!) can access the message metadata by several ways:

-   Fetch all the messages in a cannel by performaing [`conversations.history` API](https://api.slack.com/methods/conversations.history) calls with include_all_metadata argument
-   Subscribe to [`message`](https://api.slack.com/events/message) events
-   Subscribe to [`message_metadata_posted`](https://api.slack.com/events/message_metadata_posted), [`message_metadata_updated`](https://api.slack.com/events/message_metadata_updated), [`message_metadata_deleted`](https://api.slack.com/events/message_metadata_deleted) events

If you go with the message_metadata_\* events, please don't forget having the following settings in your App Manifest:

```yaml
settings:
  event_subscriptions:
    request_url: https://{your domain}/slack/events
    bot_events:
      - message_metadata_deleted
      - message_metadata_posted
      - message_metadata_updated
##### Manually add this part in the App Manifest editor at https://api.slack.com/apps 
    metadata_subscriptions:
      - app_id: "*"
        event_type: internal-procurement-approval
```

body:
## Backport

This PR is auto-generated from #12875 to be assessed for backporting due to the inclusion of the label backport/1.3.x.



The below text is copied from the body of the original PR.

---

This PR modifies raw_exec and exec to ensure the cgroup for a task
they are driving still exists during a task restart. These drivers
have the same bug but with different root cause.

For raw_exec, we were removing the cgroup in 2 places - the cpuset
manager, and in the unix containment implementation (the thing that
uses freezer cgroup to clean house). During a task restart, the
containment would remove the cgroup, and when the task runner hooks
went to start again would block on waiting for the cgroup to exist,
which will never happen, because it gets created by the cpuset manager
which only runs as an alloc pre-start hook. The fix here is to simply
not delete the cgroup in the containment implementation; killing the
PIDs is enough. The removal happens in the cpuset manager later anyway.

For exec, it's the same idea, except DestroyTask is called on task
failure, which in turn calls into libcontainer, which in turn deletes
the cgroup. In this case we do not have control over the deletion of
the cgroup, so instead we hack the cgroup back into life after the
call to DestroyTask.

All of this only applies to cgroups v2.

Fixes https://github.com/hashicorp/nomad/issues/12863

No CL because cgroupsv2 hasn't shipped yet.

## What does this PR do?
This PR adds parsing for Cisco ASA 434001 and 434003 using the precise style currently used for parsing Cisco ASA 434002.

## Why is it important?
We need parsing for ASA 434001, 434002, and 434003; right now only 434002 is supported, despite the others being substantially similar dissections.

## Checklist

<!-- Mandatory
Add a checklist of things that are required to be reviewed in order to have the PR approved

List here all the items you have verified BEFORE sending this PR. Please DO NOT remove any item, striking through those that do not apply. (Just in case, strikethrough uses two tildes. ~~Scratch this.~~)
-->

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [ ] ~~I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas~~ 
- [ ] ~~I have made corresponding changes to the documentation~~
- [ ] ~~I have made corresponding change to the default configuration files~~
- [ ] ~~I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works~~
- [x] I have added an entry in `CHANGELOG.next.asciidoc` or `CHANGELOG-developer.next.asciidoc`.

## How to test this PR locally
The PR uses the patterns specified here: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/security/asa/syslog/b_syslog/syslog-messages-400000-to-450001.html#con_7199521.
For testing the actual messages, these are sample logs:
For 434001:
<13>Apr 26 2022 10:24:37: %ASA-4-434001: SFR card not up and fail-close mode used, dropping TCP packet from outside:54.239.28.85/443 to Inside:10.12.128.89/57388

For 434003:
<13>May 30 2019 09:18:59: %ASA-4-434003: SFR requested to reset TCP connection from outside:54.239.28.85/443 to Inside:10.12.128.89/57388

Ideally a test would send these messages through filebeat with the Cisco ASA module enabled, although in this case the change is small enough to be visually inspected and compared with the working 434002 dissection that neighbors the changes and the Cisco specified log patterns from https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/security/asa/syslog/b_syslog/syslog-messages-400000-to-450001.html#con_7199521.

author: bstoll
body:
Github runners have [7GB](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-github-hosted-runners/about-github-hosted-runners#supported-runners-and-hardware-resources) of RAM allocated to them.  Static check analysis appears to exceed this limit and crashes sometimes.  This is mostly due to the large generated code in Ondatra/ygot that this repo uses heavily.

Static checks on my dev machine report the following stats:
```
/usr/bin/time -v staticcheck ./...
...
Elapsed (wall clock) time (h:mm:ss or m:ss): 10:07.36
Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 5965512
...
```

Adjusting the GOGC setting, we can lower the memory usage at the cost of some additional CPU time:
```
GOGC=30 /usr/bin/time -v staticcheck ./...
...
Elapsed (wall clock) time (h:mm:ss or m:ss): 11:14.21
Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 4088248
...
```

We can also get a big improvement by adding ~/.cache/staticcheck to the cache.  A cached run example:
```
GOGC=30 /usr/bin/time -v staticcheck ./...
...
Elapsed (wall clock) time (h:mm:ss or m:ss): 0:02.77
Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 73468
...

author: jord4n-ac
body:
In this project, I added some functionality to my application to make it interactive. The user will also be able to mark task completion by selecting the corresponding checkbox (or undo it by unchecking the checkbox). The updated tasks list gets stored in local storage.

### Project requirements & Feautures

- Add a new JavaScript file and import it as a module, it contains methods related to the status updates (completed: true/false)
- Add event listener to the checkbox
- Update items object's value for completed key upon user actions
- Implement a function for the "Clear all completed" button
- Store the updated array of items in local storage, so the user gets the correct list values when the page reloads.

#### Additional

- When the user adds a task a message saying 'Added successfully' appears, the page scrolls to show the new task and it gest highlight
- When the user adds a task that already exists a message saying 'Task repeated' appears, the page scrolls to show the repeated task and it gest highlight
- All text that the user inputs is trimmed (remove extra spaces from sides and middle), and empty text is not allowed
- When the user edits a task and adds empty text it returns the latest task
- You can add a new task, by pressing enter on input, pressing <kbd>↲</kbd> enter on Add button, or click on Add <kbd>↲</kbd> button
- You can mark a task as completed, clicking on the checkbox or pressing enter on the checkbox (This is when you want to navigate using Tab <kbd>↹</kbd> bey)


### General Requirements

- Check linter errors
- Use the correct GitHub flow
- Document my work in a professional way
- Follow best practices for HTML, CSS & JavaScript

When trying to perform a regex replace, account for the possibility of having empty strings as input.

### Why are the changes needed?
<!--

https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/29891 was merged to address https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-30796 and introduced a bug that would not allow regex matching on empty strings, as it would account for position within substring but not consider the case where input string has length 0 (empty string)

From https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-39107 there is a change in behavior between spark versions.
3.0.2
```
scala> val df = spark.sql("SELECT '' AS col")
df: org.apache.spark.sql.DataFrame = [col: string]

scala> df.withColumn("replaced", regexp_replace(col("col"), "^$", "<empty>")).show
+---+--------+
|col|replaced|
+---+--------+
|   | <empty>|
+---+--------+
```
3.1.2
```
scala> val df = spark.sql("SELECT '' AS col")
df: org.apache.spark.sql.DataFrame = [col: string]

scala> df.withColumn("replaced", regexp_replace(col("col"), "^$", "<empty>")).show
+---+--------+
|col|replaced|
+---+--------+
|   |        |
+---+--------+
```

The 3.0.2 outcome is the expected and correct one

author: camelliadpg
body:
@trilinos/intrepid2
@trilinos/kokkos

## Motivation
In [Kokkos PR 4800](https://github.com/kokkos/kokkos/pull/4800), Views were changed such that they now have compile-time operator() methods with argument counts that do not match the static rank of the operator, which violated some assumptions in the Intrepid2 `supports_rank_n` operators.  This led to build failures in Intrepid2 during Kokkos promotion, documented in [Kokkos Issue 4992](https://github.com/kokkos/kokkos/issues/4992).

This PR modifies the implementation of `supports_rank_n` to do the following:
- if the class provides a static `rank` member, then supports_rank_n will be true only if `n == rank`
- otherwise, use SFINAE as before to test whether the class implements `operator()` with `n` arguments

## Related Issues
* Closes [Kokkos Issue 4992](https://github.com/kokkos/kokkos/issues/4992).

## Testing
I have added some `static_assert` tests that check that `supports_rank_n` works as expected with Kokkos Views of ranks from 1 to 7.

author: dantemss
body:
For: https://github.com/openstax/unified/issues/1845

The images were resized using imagemagick's default settings (which seemed to produce the best balance of keeping the text readable and avoiding jagged edges).
Then the resized images and the original images were fed into ImageOptim to minimize their disk size (lossless compression).
The CTA img tag asks for 360x256 images but retina displays actually display 720x512 images instead, so a srcset attribute was added.

If desired, we could also save a further ~50% image size by passing them through ImageOptim in lossy mode with PNG quality set to 90% (the maximum).

### Summary

This commit adds a new function marginal_distribution which performs
marginalization similar to the existing marginal_counts() function. This
new function however differs in a few key ways. Most importantly the order
of the bit indices is significant for the purpose of permuting the bits
while marginalizing, while marginal_counts() doesn't do this.
Additionally, this function only works with dictionaries and not Result
objects and is written in Rust for performance. While the purposed of
this function is mostly identical to marginal_counts(), because making
the bit indices order significant is a breaking change this was done as
a separate function to avoid that. Once this new function is released
we can look at deprecated and eventually removing the existing
marginal_counts() function.

### Details and comments

Fixes #6230

author: tvolk131
body:
## Change Description
Many tests use the following assertion template:
```
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("some description: %v", err)
	}
```

which we can replace with:
```
	require.NoError(t, err, "some description")
```

This is functionally identical but more concise and, I would argue, easier to read. Performing this change reduces the size of affected test files by up to 6.5%. Not bad for something so simple!

It's also worth noting that, in order to prevent 80+ character lines, we can choose to only perform this conversion on lines with a certain description length. Looking at the replacement assertion above, and counting the tab as 8 characters as specified in the contribution guide, an assertion with an empty description is 35 characters, allowing for up to 45-character descriptions. This is why the find-and-replace regex (see below) has `[^"%]{0,45}` which allows for a description of between 1 and 45 characters.

## Don't Trust - Verify!
Sifting through all of the changes here would take a long time and be quite tedious and error-prone. It makes more sense to review _how_ I made the changes, reproduce the steps, and compare them to this PR. To do this, perform the following steps:
1. Start a new local branch in the lnd repo, branching from the same commit as this PR
2. Use VS Code's find-and-replace feature *with regex mode enabled* using the following regex:
`\n\tif err != nil \{\n\t\tt.Fatalf\("([^"%]{0,45}): %[a-z]", err\)\n\t\}\n`
and the following replacement:
`\n\trequire.NoError(t, err, "$1")\n`
and the following "files to include":
`**/**test**` (so we only modify test files)
and the following "files to exclude":
`itest,channeldb/migration*` (so we don't modify integration tests or migration code)

For me, this changed 1855 instances across 92 files. There are currently a total of 6090 calls to `t.Fatalf()`, so this accounts for 30.5% of them.
3. Add the `require` dependency (`github.com/stretchr/testify/require`) to files where it's missing - VS Code should automatically add it to most files, but for me it missed `chainntnfs/test_utils.go`, `chainntnfs/bitcoindnotify/bitcoind_test.go`, and `chainntnfs/btcdnotify/btcd_test.go`
4. Commit your changes in the local branch and compare to the commit in this PR using `git diff <commit-id> <commit-id>` - there should be no diffs

author: xfbs
body:
Hey,

I discovered a bug with the AsyncRead implementation. When you have some future that occasionally returns `Poll::Pending` (as futures do), we were seeing some amounts of null bytes in the Body output. What I found out is that what happens is this:

- The buffer for incoming data gets increased in size
- The AsyncRead part is polled
- If the AsyncRead part returns `Poll::Read(Ok(_))` or `Poll::Ready(Err(_))`, everything works as expected and the buffer is trimmed at the end
- If the AsyncRead part returns `Poll::Pending`, the [`ready!` macro](https://docs.rs/futures/latest/futures/macro.ready.html) that is being used returns early from the function, *without ever trimming the buffer*. This is where the null data comes from.

Fortunately, the fix was quite easy: just don't use that macro, but actually handle the cases. I hope this can be merged quickly.

author: sbuercklin
body:
This implements the `Partials` arithmetic with `Complex` numbers in addition to `Real`, and enables the retrieval of `partials` from `Complex{<:Dual}` numbers. 

A direct consequence of these changes is that `jacobian(f, x)` where `f` maps from R^n -> C^m works, as well as the in-place variation `jacobian!`. 

Tests are still passing and none of the differentiation methods (`gradient, jacobian, hessian`) were modified. Are there any problems generalizing the `Partials` arithmetic as I've done? My concern is that there may be some `Dual` methods which should be supported for full generality, but my local tests haven't uncovered any of them.

author: sanyuehan
body:
Hello, 
I'm a beginner but I noticed that there might be a small problem in the PrivateKey class: 
In this class, you defined balance, unspents, and transactions as public attributes, but initialized them with zero or vacant list. 
If you instantiate a prv key obj without calling get_balance()/get_unspents()/get_transactions() methods, the result of key.balance, key.unspents, key.transactions are all wrong. 
This may be misleading and may trigger potential bugs if your package is used without attention because the public attributes look like properties. 
A good solution is to make these attributes protected and create their corresponding properties, leaving the interface unchanged while solving the consistency problem, just like the self._address attribute does.

author: fkiraly
body:
Internal conversions could lead to unexpected results and breakage in a rare case where internal methods or pipeline components produced non-conformant `pd.Series`, i.e., `pandas.Series` with a name (as opposed to no name).

In that case, `convert_to` would produce an empty `pandas.DataFrame`, in line with actual (but highly unintuitive behaviour) of the `pandas` native constructor converter `pd.DataFrame(my_series, columns="col_name")`, which also produces an empty `pandas.DataFrame` if `my_series` is a `pandas.Series` with a name that is not `"col_name"`.

This PR is a bugfix for such cases, by catching this edge case properly. From now on, even if `pd.Series` with a name are provided, the column name is correctly assigned, and the content of the data frame is correctly retained.

Should fix #2604.

body: # Scope This PR includes additions to the ACF plotting, as plots for phase and power of the ACF were requested along side. I've designed it similar to the Davit plots, but without the extra info that you get from fitacf. The defaults have been changed to be un-normalized and for the power and phase to be plotted, but you can get the original by setting these to True and False respectively. I've also changed the logic a little so that the power plot does not get normalized. I've also added a return so the values of power and phase will be returned so the user can play around with them however they wish. body:
# Summary

Current version of Reactive-Resume is not working anymore, so it needs to be updated. As this is not as straight forward as I would expect, this is a Draft Pull request for others to help and comment on. Please see more details below.

# Issue description

1. App now requires a separate database docker
2. `martadinata666` fork that we were using is consuming too much memory during installation due to compilation which is giving me some issues (I would expect others to have the same problem)
3. Moving to the official version, it splits the app into 2 sections: Server (API) and Client (Webpage)
4. A reverse proxy app is required to properly route API and Clients requests
5. For images it requires a S3 cloud server as it doesn't save it locally at the moment
6. PDF is currently not working (at least I couldn't get it to work)
7. The latest version is not running on ARM devices due to `playwright` dependency not having an ARM version

# 1) Database [DONE]

As it now requires multiple dockers, I've created a stack and included POSTGRES docker in it, solving the issue

# 2) and 3) Issues with `martadinata666` fork [COMMENTS WELCOMED]

I didn't have much luck with it, but it could have being only me. Although I believe using the official one would be better and it's quicker to deploy (and I would imagine update).

As we already require a stack, I don't see it adding much more complexity.

# 4) Reverse Proxy [FEEDBACK REQUIRED]

There are options using NPM, Nginx and Traefik.
The simplest one would be to use Traefik as it can be configured within the stack and wouldn't require any additional steps. That being said, I don't have much experience with Traefik and I'm afraid it could mess up with others configuration. Also, using users own domain is not the most straight forward thing with Traefik.
The other option would be to include an nginx container into the pack. But it would require a separate file to be installed and modified for the users own domain. It could be easily done with a pre-install script.
The third option (the one I'm using here) is to create a documentation explaining for the user the 3 different software to be used and how to configure on each of them. So if they have already NPM or Traefik running (which I would imagine to be the case) they don't need an extra container running.

The only thing is that SERVER needs to be configured as a `/api` path of the domain used on the client for the app to work properly. That's why this part is important to be done correctly.

References:
- https://github.com/AmruthPillai/Reactive-Resume/blob/main/docker-compose.yml
- https://hub.docker.com/r/martadinata666/reactive-resume

# 5) Cloud Service [HELP NEEDED]

The app does run without a Cloud service, but no image can be uploaded. This is not the end of the world, but it does reduces a bit the app functionality.
One can use any cloud provider out there (AWS, Digital Ocean, Etc..), but in my opinion it does defeat the purpose of a self-hosted app.

I'm trying to use MinIO container as a self hosted S3 replacement, but for some reason it's not working fine with Reactive-Resume. I don't know if that is me doing something wrong or some other issue within Reactive-Resume app.

Reference: https://github.com/AmruthPillai/Reactive-Resume/issues/829#issue-1198991026

# 6) PDF issue [I'VE IGNORED AT THE MOMENT]

As this seams to be an issue within the app and should get resolved on their end, there is not much to do other than wait.

Reference: https://github.com/AmruthPillai/Reactive-Resume/issues/721#issue-1171058045

# 7) Latest version doesn't have ARM [REFERENCE ONLY]

There is not much to do (in my opinion) other than use an older version until they managed to sort on their end. This does mean that if the PDF issue got sorted we will not have it until this get sorted as well.

Reference: https://github.com/AmruthPillai/Reactive-Resume/pull/817#issuecomment-1092556488


# Conclusion

I'm posting here what I've achieved so far and the issues I've faced/resolved. Any comments and/or further support is welcome.

author: kimvsparrow
body:
A metric for Requests makes a lot more sense in Datadog (presumably other Statsd consumers as well) when typed as a Count type instead of a Gauge.  Datadog doesn't do a great job of transforming gauges into a rate.

Puma tallies the total number of requests it has handled since start.  This change tracks the previously reported total, and subtracts that from the current total, for a count of requests since the previous report.  Then we can change the type of the metric.

While this change makes sense to me, I'd consider it a breaking change.  It will require changes in monitoring from other users who already depend on the Gauge type.  So it's understandable if this doesn't fit in with your plans.

P.S.  I dig the recent Unix domain socket change.  I had to jump through some hoops to get around this same issue in our own infrastructure!

While this is generally good, it seems to have broken the Windows build for Shapely-1.8 somehow (it could be a bug with Windows). This PR restores "pip install" with [`--no-use-pep517`](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/cli/pip_install/#cmdoption-use-pep517) to force legacy behaviour (i.e. ignores `pyproject.toml`). The other change is that `GEOS_LIBRARY_PATH` can be commented out for now, as this was only used by `shapely._buildcfg.py`, which is no longer used. (I think this is used for shapely-2.0, so keep it as a comment for now).

body:
I couldn't find any evidence of any of the styles in `covid.styl` being actually used by the covid project. They're global definitions and some are quite generic (like `.footer`), so they can interfere with styling elsewhere. So deleting them would be nice.

FYI, my searches that turned up nothing:
```bash
$ git grep shieldlist content/projects/covid19
$ git grep feature content/projects/covid19
$ git grep paper content/projects/covid19
$ git grep footer content/projects/covid19
```
Since all the styles in the file depend on those classes, I concluded that nothing was using these rules. But please let me know if you notice something broken.

* api-change:``ec2``: This release adds support to query the public key and creation date of EC2 Key Pairs. Additionally, the format (pem or ppk) of a key pair can be specified when creating a new key pair.
* api-change:``braket``: This release enables Braket Hybrid Jobs with Embedded Simulators to have multiple instances.
* api-change:``guardduty``: Documentation update for API description.
* api-change:``connect``: This release introduces an API for changing the current agent status of a user in Connect.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.25.2
   ```
   ======

* api-change:``rekognition``: This release adds support to configure stream-processor resources for label detections on streaming-videos. UpateStreamProcessor API is also launched with this release, which could be used to update an existing stream-processor.
* api-change:``cloudtrail``: Increases the retention period maximum to 2557 days. Deprecates unused fields of the ListEventDataStores API response. Updates documentation.
* api-change:``lookoutequipment``: This release adds the following new features: 1) Introduces an option for automatic schema creation 2) Now allows for Ingestion of data containing most common errors and allows automatic data cleaning 3) Introduces new API ListSensorStatistics that gives further information about the ingested data
* api-change:``iotwireless``: Add list support for event configurations, allow to get and update event configurations by resource type, support LoRaWAN events; Make NetworkAnalyzerConfiguration as a resource, add List, Create, Delete API support; Add FCntStart attribute support for ABP WirelessDevice.

* api-change:``chime-sdk-media-pipelines``: For Amazon Chime SDK meetings, the Amazon Chime Media Pipelines SDK allows builders to capture audio, video, and content share streams. You can also capture meeting events, live transcripts, and data messages. The pipelines save the artifacts to an Amazon S3 bucket that you designate.
* api-change:``sagemaker``: Amazon SageMaker Autopilot adds support for custom validation dataset and validation ratio through the CreateAutoMLJob and DescribeAutoMLJob APIs.

* api-change:``sagemaker``: SageMaker Inference Recommender now accepts customer KMS key ID for encryption of endpoints and compilation outputs created during inference recommendation.
* api-change:``pricing``: Documentation updates for Price List API
* api-change:``glue``: This release adds documentation for the APIs to create, read, delete, list, and batch read of AWS Glue custom patterns, and for Lake Formation configuration settings in the AWS Glue crawler.
* api-change:``cloudfront``: CloudFront now supports the Server-Timing header in HTTP responses sent from CloudFront. You can use this header to view metrics that help you gain insights about the behavior and performance of CloudFront. To use this header, enable it in a response headers policy.
* api-change:``ivschat``: Adds new APIs for IVS Chat, a feature for building interactive chat experiences alongside an IVS broadcast.

will need to rely on. By itself it does not provide any function to the end user.

Possible uses of this module can be:

* Add subcontracted services to BOMs. When a manufacturing order is created a
  PO is triggered for the service to be subcontracted. See

* Add subcontracted services to sales order. When the SO is confirmed, it
  creates a PO for the service.

author: psteckler
body:
The `Snark_work_received` structured log in `Snark_pool_diff` was causing errors because the `work` field had JSON that could not be parsed. The parse failure was due to a reversal of the fields in the JSON for fee excesses.

I was unable to track down where that reversal occurred, perhaps it's something internal in the Yojson library. `Fee_excess.to_yojson` produces a particular field order, and the only instance I could find where we construct such JSON manually, the fields are in the right order.

The solution here is to allow `of_yojson` to accept either order of the fields, per Postel's Law.

Closes #10849. Verified that the unparseable JSON mentioned in that issue becomes parseable after this change.

author: github-learning-lab[bot]
body:
# Welcome to Managing Merge Conflicts :tada: Hello, and welcome! If you're here to learn about and practice resolving merge conflicts, you're in the right place. In this course, you'll learn why merge conflicts happen and solve a few of them. The merge conflicts in this course are simple enough to solve from GitHub.com. But, if you'd prefer, you can solve them using the command line or other local tools. As an added bonus, the project we are using for this course is a resume hosted on [GitHub Pages](https://help.github.com/en/categories/github-pages-basics)! So, if you want to keep working after you complete this course, please feel free! Before starting this course, we recommend completing the [Introduction to GitHub Learning Lab](https://lab.github.com/githubtraining/introduction-to-github) first. > Note: You may notice that some branches and pull requests already exist. We'll be using them in later activities in this course. ### How merge conflicts happen A **Merge conflict** occurs when changes are made to the same part of the same file on two different branches. You usually find out about conflicts in a pull request. This can be intimidating, but have no fear, Git knows how to handle this! It only needs a human to decide how to resolve the conflict. ## Step 1: Resolve a simple conflict You may merge a lot of pull requests before you encounter your first merge conflict. That’s because Git is smart when it comes to merging. Unless you're paying close attention to other branches, you won't know about conflicts until you create a pull request. This branch is a great example. In this scenario, two of our friends have been working in this repository. They both created branches, made changes to the `_config.yml` file, and opened pull requests. One pull request was merged to `main` without problems, but now the other pull request has a conflict. The history of `main` and this branch look something like this: ![deviated branches](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13326548/36703493-b8f4d5ee-1b10-11e8-9f95-4ec9993fe704.png) Because this pull request changes the same lines in the `_config.yml` file, there is a merge conflict. Let's help our friends resolve this conflict. ### :keyboard: Activity: Resolving your first merge conflict 1. At the bottom of the page in the "This branch has conflicts that must be resolved" section of the Pull Request, click the **Resolve conflicts** button. 2. Look for the highlighted sections that begins with `<<<<<<< update-config` and ends with `>>>>>>> main`. These markers are added by Git to show you the content that is in conflict. 3. Remove the changes made on the main branch by deleting all of the content below the `=======` and above `>>>>>>> main`. 4. Next, remove the merge conflict markers by deleting the following lines: <<<<<<< update-config ======= >>>>>>> main 5. With the merge conflict markers removed, click **Mark as resolved**. 6. Finally, click **Commit merge**. > Sometimes, the best way to resolve a merge conflict is to add content that's from both branches, or even something that isn't on either! This is why Git needs a human to look at the code and make the proper fixes.

Watch below for my response.

author: guilhermocc
body:
## What ❓
Implement a reliable queue pattern for operations. Every pending operation taken from the queue to be processed by the worker will now reside in an auxiliary queue before being taken from the channel so we can prevent operations loss if the worker goes down at that moment.

## Why 🤔  
Currently, we always pop an operation from the queue before actually executing it. If the worker component goes down in the meantime, these operations will no longer be in the queue and will remain in pending operation forever without lease data.

author: gerow
body:
C_GetAttributeValue should return CKR_ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_INVALID in the case
that one or more of the attributes requested aren't valid for the given
object, so this fixes that.

When using gnutls this actually manifests as a segfault, as it assumes
in the CKR_OK case that all the returned buffers are valid, but p11-kit
"helpfully" sets the "length" value for invalid buffers to -1, which
gnutls interprets as a uint, which means it tries to read a very large
amount of memory before eventually failing.

Addresses part of #21.

author: danielhollas
body:
When I refactored force_abin in #109, I deleted a bit of obscure logic in `read_forces()` that allowed skipping forces. 
Turns out this logic was needed for SH, since in `sh_init` we were calling the interface and requesting only energies without forces.  Hence, that change broke the MOLPRO-SH interface. I could reintroduce the hack or solve it in some other way, but it felt easier for now to simply calculate the forces, even though we throw them out in `sh_init`.

I have also added a workaround for a compiler bug that is specific for the Gfortran 7.3 (which happens to be installed on PHOTOX clusters unfortunately). The workaround is needed in the error paths in the file interface in case energies or forces could not be read. Before the workaround, the `inquire` statement that we are using to get the filename from the file unit would result in an ugly and confusing runtime error.
